referees.quote: I recommend the manuscript for publication in Nature Communications. The only change that needs to be made is that they use the acronym SFAL ... before it is defined

Before further consideration, I suggest that the authors provide a more rigorous reconciliation of the discrepancy between the theoretical model and the experimental results; and use a precise physical definition
the manuscript has many overclaims and even misconception, which make it unacceptable for the high standard of Nat. Comm. ... the current manuscript does not meet the high standard of Nat. Comm.

note: First round is Version 0 in this file; nothing indicates a transfer from another journal. No referee co-signed another's report. R1 asked to publish with only an acronym fix, which maps to minor revision under the stated rule. R2 asked for substantial theoretical reconciliation or retreat from claims plus toned-down terminology, so major revision. R3 judged the paper unsuitable for the journal, so reject. R2 did not take part in later rounds. In later rounds R1 asked for further revision and then recommended publication after minor corrections; R3 kept rejecting in Version 1 and found it suitable for publication in Version 2.
